note: Selected verified evidence connections, not an exhaustive benchmark assignment or reproduced leaderboard.

entries.evidence: FaSTA* §5.1 uses 121 image-prompt pairs with 550 operations and human subtask scoring; Appendix A MagicBrush evidence is qualitative.
entries.caveat: Do not label this the standard MagicBrush quantitative score.

entries.evidence: §4 constructs 16 degradation combinations and separates exploration images from testing; evaluates fidelity and no-reference quality.
entries.caveat: A constructed restoration test, not a general instruction-editing benchmark.

entries.evidence: Abstract and §IV explicitly identify both datasets.
entries.caveat: Record single/multi-turn settings and judge configuration when using scores.

entries.evidence: Official README performance section names all four.
entries.caveat: Distinct editing backbones and thinker variants should not be collapsed.

entries.evidence: Abstract introduces LGBench and identifies GenEval and ImgEdit results.
entries.caveat: Training-free supervisor and GRPO-trained planner are separate configurations.

entries.evidence: Abstract establishes native high-definition dialogue evaluation and stepwise targets.
entries.caveat: Native-resolution consistency is distinct from resized image quality.

entries.evidence: Main experiments and Appendix B report these respective evaluations.
entries.caveat: Declarative programs and generative tool calls coexist; disclose tool access and replanning budgets.

entries.evidence: §5.1 names three benchmarks; Appendix G describes modified or reimplemented agent baselines.
entries.caveat: Avoid claiming universal superiority based on modified baseline configurations or changed judges.

entries.evidence: Primary abstract identifies synthetic and real subsets with downstream perception evaluation.
entries.caveat: Driving-perception restoration has a different objective from creative editing.

entries.evidence: Abstract identifies compositional generation and scene decomposition compared with compute-matched parallel sampling.
entries.caveat: Specify the measured categories; not all figures represent the entire benchmark.

entries.evidence: §5.1 uses a combined 500-sample test, not either full benchmark, with standardized images and restricted instruction lengths.
entries.caveat: Do not report as the complete standard MagicBrush or CompBench protocol.

entries.evidence: Official proceedings abstract explicitly identifies both benchmarks.
entries.caveat: Do not substitute the later RISEBench++ protocol.

entries.evidence: Paper §§3–5: 200-prompt AgentDrawBench; structural checklists, perceptual criteria and pairwise preference.
entries.caveat: Zero-shot permits multiple execution turns. Structural fidelity and perceptual quality differ; GUI is a comparison, not coding.

entries.evidence: Introduces MaLiang-IBench and MaLiang-VBench; reports delivery, quality and cost.
entries.caveat: Only its image track is surveyed here; runnable output is distinct from satisfying visual requirements.

entries.evidence: Primary abstract separates proposal-feedback and candidate-selection tasks, then tests held-out MultiBanana tasks.
entries.caveat: Cross-task harness search is distinct from revising one image; prevent selection/test leakage.

entries.evidence: Primary abstract reports BlenderGym, SlideBench and introduced BlenderBench.
entries.caveat: Only image/document reconstruction and the render-inspect mechanism are in scope.

entries.evidence: LEGO-Bench separates artifact validity, visible geometry and appearance.
entries.caveat: Single-view reconstruction cannot establish correctness of hidden geometry; broader vision readouts are contextual.

entries.evidence: Primary abstract gives benchmark and agent together and separates workflow design from task resolution.
entries.caveat: ComfyBench includes modalities beyond images; use its image-relevant tasks and do not interpret execution success as instruction satisfaction.

entries.evidence: Primary abstract identifies the module interface, hierarchical planning and evaluation on three public benchmarks.
entries.caveat: General-purpose generation spans multiple tasks; the graph/module interface is more constrained than arbitrary source-code synthesis.

entries.evidence: Full-text §§3–4 identifies code backends and task-specific evaluations; physical-simulation examples are qualitative.
entries.caveat: A correct draft does not guarantee neural final pixels preserve every relation; report generator and agent backbone separately.

entries.evidence: Full-text §4 and appendices evaluate graph/workflow agents on compositional and multilingual prompt suites.
entries.caveat: The paper uses a particular VLM judge implementation; prompt and sampler edits dominate many runs, so graph-editing availability is not identical to frequent structural edits.

entries.evidence: Primary abstract verifies these three modules and MatPlotBench.
entries.caveat: Model-based visual ratings do not by themselves guarantee correct data transformation.

entries.evidence: Primary abstract verifies Parser, Planner and Painter–Commenter loop plus editable PPTX output.
entries.caveat: Its PosterAgent is distinct from Yu et al. 2026 PosterAgent trained with SARL.

entries.evidence: Primary abstract verifies the two agents and separate fidelity/editability evaluation across several artifact types.
entries.caveat: Visual reconstruction and usable editability must be evaluated separately; they can trade off.

entries.evidence: Primary full text sections 4 and Appendix M specify the code layout, critique/refinement and aesthetic-rendering stages.
entries.caveat: The original system does not make every synthesized icon editable; AutoFigure-Edit is a distinct extension.

entries.evidence: Primary abstract separates request-level print-ready rate, native editability, and aesthetic scores conditioned on successful outputs; official repository confirms rendering and review stages.
entries.caveat: Print-ready rate is defined by the paper-specific checks; conditional aesthetics must not conceal failed requests or establish universal production readiness.

benchmarks: Qualitative case studies; no named quantitative benchmark verified
entries.evidence: Full-text §2 describes DOM layers and real text; §3 supplies comparative cases, showcases and replay trajectories.
entries.caveat: Evidence is qualitative case study/showcase; there is no named quantitative benchmark in §3. Do not assert universal production-grade success.
